mainTopic: חולין שנשחטו בעזרה and קידושין, money from forbidden items, and whether טובת הנאה is money
overview: The ברייתא widens the איסור of חולין שנשחטו בעזרה to cover בעלי מומין, חיה and עופות. It also forbids any benefit from such meat, not just eating it. מר יהודה then quotes רבי שמעון, who says קידושין with this meat works, and contrasts it with רבי שמעון's ruling that the meat must be burned. רבה resolves the contradiction: the קידושין case is about an animal that turned out to be a טריפה, and for רבי שמעון that animal is not forbidden for benefit. Next the גמרא explains why money from selling forbidden items may be used for קידושין. Only עבודה זרה and שביעית pass their status on to the money, and the גמרא shows how שביעית status moves along a chain of trades. A new משנה then rules that a ישראל can betroth with תרומות, מעשרות and other gifts. This leads to a debate over whether טובת הנאה counts as money. עולא explains the משנה as an inheritance from a כהן grandfather, so the משנה cannot prove the question either way.

steps.title: Blemished animals are included in the prohibition
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא extends the איסור of slaughtering חולין in the עזרה to blemished animals, because they belong to a kind that is fit for the מזבח.
steps.simpleTranslation: [So far we only know this rule for animals] that are fit to be offered. How do we know to include blemished animals? I include them, since they are of a kind that is fit to be offered.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues from the previous daf. It has proven that חולין slaughtered in the עזרה are forbidden, and now it starts widening the rule, beginning with בעלי מומין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A blemished animal cannot itself be brought as a קרבן. But its species (cattle, sheep, goats) is a קרבן species. That family connection is enough to include it in the איסור.

keyTerms.meaning: Animals fit to be offered as a קרבן
Blemished animals, which may not be offered
To include (in a rule)
A kind or species that is fit (for the מזבח)

phrases.english: [I only know this for animals] that are fit to be offered.
From where do we know to include blemished animals?
I include blemished animals,
since they are of the kind that is fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא begun on the previous daf
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Blemished animals slaughtered in the עזרה are included in the איסור, because their species is fit for קרבנות.

steps.title: Undomesticated animals are included too
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא includes a חיה, because it needs שחיטה just like a בהמה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how do we know to include an undomesticated animal? I include it, because it is made permitted by slaughtering, just like a domesticated animal.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא widens the rule another step and includes חיה (deer and similar animals).
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חיה can never be a קרבן, so the 'fit species' reason from step 1 does not work here. Instead, the link is that a חיה is made kosher through שחיטה, exactly like a בהמה.

keyTerms.meaning: An undomesticated kosher animal, such as a deer
A domesticated animal, such as cattle, sheep or goats
Kosher ritual slaughter

phrases.english: And from where do we know to include the undomesticated animal?
I include the undomesticated animal,
since it is [made permitted] by slaughtering, like a domesticated animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a further category using a new reason
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A חיה slaughtered in the עזרה is included, because it requires שחיטה like a בהמה.

steps.title: Birds are included from the verses
steps.stepSummary: For birds the ברייתא cannot use logic alone, so it brings a פסוק: the repeated phrases about slaughtering.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know to include birds? The verse says: 'And he slaughters it,' 'and he shall slaughter it,' 'and he shall slaughter it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא includes עופות in the איסור. This time it relies on extra words in the פסוקים instead of a logical comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasons used for בעלי מומין and חיה do not cleanly fit birds, so a תלמוד לומר is needed. The repeated words about slaughtering 'it' are read as extra, and that extra wording is what brings in birds.

keyTerms.meaning: Birds
'The verse teaches': introduces a proof from a פסוק
'And he shall slaughter it'

steps.whatToRemember: The איסור of חולין slaughtered in the עזרה covers kosher animals fit for קרבנות, blemished animals, חיה, and birds.

phrases.english: From where do we know to include birds?
The verse states: 'And he slaughters it,'
'and he shall slaughter it,' 'and he shall slaughter it.'
phrases.notes: The ברייתא treats these three mentions of slaughtering 'it' as extra words that come to include birds.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Final inclusion, based on a פסוק rather than logic
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Birds slaughtered in the עזרה are also included, learned from the repeated slaughtering phrases.

steps.title: Even benefit from the meat is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא teaches that חולין slaughtered in the עזרה may not even be thrown to dogs. Benefit is forbidden, not just eating.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might think it is only forbidden to slaughter it there, but once slaughtered you may throw it to the dogs. The verse says: 'To the dog you shall throw it.' It, a טריפה, you may throw to the dog, but you may not throw חולין slaughtered in the עזרה.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא raises a possible mistake: maybe only eating is forbidden. It rejects that and teaches that no benefit at all is allowed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about טריפה says to throw 'it' to the dog, meaning benefit from a טריפה is allowed. The word 'it' is read as limiting: only the טריפה may go to the dogs. חולין slaughtered in the עזרה are excluded, so they are אסור בהנאה.

keyTerms.meaning: 'One might think': introduces a wrong assumption
'To the dog you shall throw it'
Non-sacred animals slaughtered in the Temple courtyard
The Temple courtyard

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the basis for the next question. If benefit is forbidden, can this meat be used for קידושין?

phrases.english: One might think: he should not slaughter [there],
but if he did slaughter, he may throw it to the dogs?
The verse states: 'To the dog you shall throw it'
It you may throw to the dog,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי אַתָּה מַשְׁלִיךְ חוּלִּין שֶׁנִּשְׁחֲטוּ בַּעֲזָרָה.
phrases.english: but you may not throw non-sacred animals slaughtered in the courtyard.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָכוֹל לֹא יִשְׁחוֹט וְאִם שָׁחַט יַשְׁלִיכֶנּוּ לִפְנֵי כְלָבִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Expands the איסור from eating to all benefit
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חולין slaughtered in the עזרה are forbidden for all benefit, learned from 'אותו' in the פסוק of טריפה.

steps.title: מר יהודה cites a dispute about betrothal with forbidden items
steps.stepSummary: מר יהודה meets רב יוסף and רב שמואל and quotes a ברייתא: קידושין with פטר חמור, בשר בחלב, or חולין slaughtered in the עזרה works according to רבי שמעון but not according to חכמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: מר יהודה found רב יוסף and רב שמואל son of רבה בר בר חנה standing at the entrance of רבה's study hall. He said to them: It was taught: one who betroths with a firstborn donkey, with meat cooked in milk, or with חולין slaughtered in the עזרה: רבי שמעון says she is betrothed, and the חכמים say she is not.
steps.whatsHappening: A short story introduces a new discussion. מר יהודה quotes a ברייתא about using forbidden items for קידושין, setting up a question about רבי שמעון's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All three items are commonly treated as אסור בהנאה. For קידושין the woman must receive something of value. The dispute is about whether these items count as valuable.

keyTerms.meaning: One who betroths a woman
A firstborn donkey
Meat cooked in milk
She is betrothed
'It was taught': introduces a ברייתא

phrases.english: Mar Yehuda found Rav Yosef

phrases.aramaic: וּלְרַב שְׁמוּאֵל בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה
phrases.english: and Rav Shmuel, son of Rabba bar bar Chana,
who were standing at the entrance of Rabba's study hall.
He said to them: It was taught:
One who betroths with a firstborn donkey,
with meat in milk,
or with non-sacred animals slaughtered in the courtyard:
Rabbi Shimon says: she is betrothed,
and the Rabbis say: she is not betrothed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the איסור itself to its effect on קידושין
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי שמעון holds קידושין with these items is valid; חכמים hold it is not.

steps.title: Inference: רבי שמעון holds the prohibition is not from the Torah
steps.stepSummary: From the ברייתא, מר יהודה concludes that according to רבי שמעון, the איסור of חולין slaughtered in the עזרה is not דאורייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: It seems, then, that according to רבי שמעון, חולין slaughtered in the עזרה are not forbidden by Torah law.
steps.whatsHappening: מר יהודה draws a conclusion from the ברייתא he just quoted. This conclusion is about to be challenged.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If an item were forbidden for benefit מדאורייתא, it would have no value and קידושין with it would fail. Since רבי שמעון says the קידושין works, he must hold the איסור is only rabbinic. The next step challenges this with a different ruling of רבי שמעון.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Apparently': introduces an inference
Not from Torah law

phrases.english: Apparently, non-sacred animals slaughtered in the courtyard
according to Rabbi Shimon are not [forbidden] by Torah law.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַלְמָא חוּלִּין שֶׁנִּשְׁחֲטוּ בַּעֲזָרָה לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a conclusion about רבי שמעון from the ברייתא
steps.raayaObject: That רבי שמעון holds the איסור of חולין slaughtered in the עזרה is not דאורייתא
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי שמעון's ruling that קידושין with such meat is valid

steps.title: Contradiction: רבי שמעון says the meat must be burned
steps.stepSummary: מר יהודה contrasts this with another ברייתא where רבי שמעון rules that such meat, including a חיה, must be burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: And he raised a contradiction: רבי שמעון says: חולין slaughtered in the עזרה must be burned, and so too a חיה slaughtered in the עזרה.
steps.whatsHappening: מר יהודה points out another ברייתא where רבי שמעון seems to hold the opposite. In that ברייתא he treats this meat strictly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Requiring burning shows that the meat is fully forbidden and cannot be used. That fits a Torah-level איסור, not the lenient view inferred in step 6. So the two statements of רבי שמעון appear to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And he contrasted them': introduces a contradiction between sources
They must be burned

phrases.english: And he raised a contradiction:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן אוֹמֵר: חוּלִּין שֶׁנִּשְׁחֲטוּ בַּעֲזָרָה
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon says: non-sacred animals slaughtered in the courtyard
must be burned,
and so too an undomesticated animal slaughtered in the courtyard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the inference of step 6 with a conflicting statement of רבי שמעון
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that רבי שמעון holds the איסור is not דאורייתא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי שמעון requires burning, which shows a full איסור הנאה. That fits a Torah prohibition, not a rabbinic one.

steps.title: They were silent
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף and רב שמואל had no answer to the contradiction.
steps.simpleTranslation: They were silent.
steps.whatsHappening: The two listeners cannot resolve the contradiction themselves. The next step brings it to רבה, who answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Silence means רב יוסף and רב שמואל had no answer of their own. Nothing has been decided yet about רבי שמעון's real view. Step 9 resolves the conflict between the two ברייתות.

keyTerms.meaning: They were silent

steps.confusionAlert: Silence does not mean רבי שמעון's position was proven wrong. It only means these listeners had no answer at that moment.

phrases.english: They were silent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Records that the contradiction went unanswered
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רב יוסף and רב שמואל could not answer the contradiction, so they bring it to רבה in the next step.

steps.title: רבה explains the first ברייתא is about a טריפה
steps.stepSummary: רבה answers the contradiction: the ברייתא about קידושין speaks of an animal slaughtered in the עזרה that turned out to be a טריפה. רבי שמעון follows his own reasoning about such a שחיטה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They came before רבה. He said to them: a quarrelsome person put you up to this question. What case are we dealing with here? One where the animal was slaughtered and then found to be a טריפה, and רבי שמעון follows his usual reasoning.
steps.whatsHappening: The students bring the unanswered contradiction to רבה, and he resolves it. He says the first ברייתא is talking about a special case, an animal that turned out to be a טריפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The contradiction was: in one ברייתא רבי שמעון lets you use חולין slaughtered in the עזרה (for קידושין), and in another he says it must be burned. רבה limits the first ברייתא to a טריפה. For רבי שמעון, a שחיטה that does not make the animal fit to eat is not a real שחיטה, so the animal never gets the status of חולין slaughtered in the עזרה.

keyTerms.meaning: A quarrelsome or divisive person, someone who likes to stir up arguments
What case are we dealing with here? Used to limit a source to a specific case
An animal with a fatal defect, which may not be eaten even after a proper שחיטה
Following his own reasoning, consistent with his view elsewhere

steps.confusionAlert: רבה is not saying רבי שמעון allows benefit from every animal slaughtered in the עזרה. Normally רבי שמעון says it must be burned. Only a טריפה escapes that rule for him.

phrases.english: They came before Rabba.
phrases.notes: "They" are רב יוסף and רב שמואל, who could not answer מר יהודה's question.

phrases.english: He said to them: A quarrelsome person has put you up to this.
phrases.notes: He means מר יהודה, who raised the challenge. The letter in square brackets is how the corrected wording spells the word.

phrases.english: Here, what case are we dealing with?
phrases.notes: "Here" means the first ברייתא, where the קידושין works according to רבי שמעון.

phrases.english: Where it was slaughtered and found to be a tereifa.
And Rabbi Shimon follows his own reasoning.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction that רב יוסף and רב שמואל could not resolve in Step 8.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the case (אוקימתא): the first ברייתא is about a טריפה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought the first ברייתא meant any animal slaughtered in the עזרה, which would contradict רבי שמעון's ruling that it must be burned.
steps.terutzMaskana: The first ברייתא is only about a טריפה, which for רבי שמעון never becomes forbidden as חולין בעזרה. So there is no contradiction.

steps.title: A ברייתא proves רבי שמעון's view on a slaughtered טריפה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי שמעון allows benefit from a טריפה slaughtered in the עזרה, while the חכמים forbid it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As taught in a ברייתא: one who slaughters a known טריפה, or slaughters an animal that turns out to be a טריפה, when both are חולין in the עזרה: רבי שמעון allows benefit and the חכמים forbid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to prove that רבי שמעון really holds this view about a טריפה, as רבה just claimed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא states outright that רבי שמעון allows benefit from a טריפה slaughtered in the עזרה. This backs up רבה's answer: the קידושין in the first ברייתא can work with such an animal, because for רבי שמעון it is not forbidden for benefit. The חכמים disagree and forbid it either way.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא; introduces a supporting source
This and that, meaning both cases
Allows a person to benefit from it

steps.whatToRemember: רבי שמעון: a טריפה slaughtered in the עזרה is not forbidden for benefit, so it can be used for קידושין. חכמים: it is forbidden for benefit.

phrases.english: As it is taught in a baraita:
One who slaughters a tereifa
and likewise one who slaughters and it was found to be a tereifa,
when this one and that one were non-sacred animals in the Temple courtyard:
Rabbi Shimon permits benefit from them,
and the Rabbis forbid it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source showing that רבי שמעון holds the view רבה relied on in Step 9.
steps.raayaObject: רבה's claim that רבי שמעון allows benefit from a טריפה slaughtered in the עזרה
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא (תוספתא חולין) where רבי שמעון permits benefit and the חכמים forbid

steps.title: What is the source that money from forbidden items is allowed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's rule that if he sold forbidden items and was מקדש with the money, the קידושין works. It asks how we know this.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he sold them and was מקדש with the money he got for them, she is מקודשת. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה and asks for its source. This sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The items themselves are אסורים בהנאה, so a woman cannot be מקודשת with them. The משנה says the money from selling them is different and may be used. The גמרא wants to know why the money does not take on the forbidden status of the items.

keyTerms.meaning: Their money, the payment received for them
She is betrothed; the קידושין works
From where do we know this? A request for a source

phrases.english: If he sold them and betrothed with their money, she is betrothed.
phrases.notes: This is a line from the משנה. "Them" means the items you may not benefit from that the משנה listed.

phrases.english: From where do we know this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the רבי שמעון discussion and opens a new topic from the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that money received for items forbidden for benefit is itself permitted

steps.title: Learning from the verse about idol worship
steps.stepSummary: The תורה tells us that money from עבודה זרה is forbidden like the idol itself. That implies the money from all other forbidden items is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תורה revealed about עבודה זרה: "And you shall be banned like it." Anything you get from it is like it. This implies that for all other forbidden items in the תורה, the money is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק about עבודה זרה. Because the תורה had to say specifically that the money of עבודה זרה is forbidden, other forbidden items must be different.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק "והיית חרם כמהו" is read as: whatever comes from the idol, such as its sale money, is forbidden like it. The תורה needed to say this for עבודה זרה. That shows the rule is not automatic, so with other forbidden items the money stays permitted. This is learned by implication (מכלל).

keyTerms.meaning: The תורה revealed, taught something explicitly
Something banned and forbidden
Bring into being, produce something from it, such as money from a sale
By implication, learning one thing from what the text says about another

phrases.english: From the fact that the Merciful One revealed regarding idol worship:
"And you shall be banned like it,"
anything that you produce from it
phrases.notes: He means things you get in exchange for the idol, such as the money from selling it.

phrases.english: is like it,
which implies that with all other prohibitions in the Torah, it is permitted.
phrases.notes: "It" means the money received for them, not the forbidden items themselves.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the מנלן question of Step 11.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Since the תורה had to forbid the money of עבודה זרה explicitly, the money of other forbidden items is permitted.

steps.title: Why not learn the rule from idol worship for everything
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: instead of treating עבודה זרה as an exception, why not learn from it that money from every forbidden item is also forbidden?
steps.simpleTranslation: But let us learn from it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last answer. It asks why עבודה זרה should not serve as a model for all forbidden items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The previous step read עבודה זרה as the exception. The challenge says the opposite reading is possible: one example can teach a general rule, so all forbidden items would pass their status to their money. Then the משנה's קידושין with the money would not work.

keyTerms.meaning: But let us learn from it, a challenge to apply one case to others

phrases.english: But let us derive from it!
phrases.notes: Learn from עבודה זרה that the money of every forbidden item is forbidden too.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading in Step 12 that עבודה זרה is an exception.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference in Step 12 that the money of other forbidden items is permitted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One example in the תורה can teach a general rule. So עבודה זרה should teach that all forbidden items pass their status to their money, not the opposite.

steps.title: Two verses that teach the same thing do not teach others
steps.stepSummary: עבודה זרה and שביעית both have a rule that their money takes on their status. Two פסוקים that teach the same thing are not used to teach other cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because עבודה זרה and שביעית are two פסוקים that teach the same thing, and any two פסוקים that teach the same thing do not teach other cases.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with a rule for learning from the תורה: when two places teach the same law, that law stays limited to those two cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the תורה wanted this rule for every forbidden item, it would not have needed to say it twice, once for עבודה זרה and once for שביעית. Saying it twice shows these two are exceptions. So the money of all other forbidden items stays permitted, and the משנה's קידושין works.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce of the שמיטה year, the seventh year
Two פסוקים that teach the same law
They do not teach, meaning they are not applied to other cases

steps.whatToRemember: Money from selling forbidden items is permitted, so a woman can be מקודשת with it. The only exceptions are עבודה זרה and שביעית, and as שני כתובים הבאים כאחד they do not teach other cases.
steps.whyThisMatters: The rule of שני כתובים הבאים כאחד אין מלמדין is a basic principle for how the גמרא learns laws from the תורה, and it appears in many places in ש״ס.

phrases.english: Because idol worship and the Sabbatical Year
are two verses that come as one,
and any two verses that come as one
do not teach to other cases.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם דְּהָוֵה עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה וּשְׁבִיעִית שְׁנֵי כְתוּבִים הַבָּאִים כְּאֶחָד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 13 and confirms the inference of Step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A rule for learning from פסוקים: two passages teaching the same law do not teach other cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might have learned from עבודה זרה that every forbidden item's money is forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: עבודה זרה and שביעית are שני כתובים הבאים כאחד, so they are exceptions, and the money of all other forbidden items is permitted.

steps.title: Where do we learn the money rule for שביעית?
steps.stepSummary: The source for עבודה זרה was already given. The גמרא now asks for the source for שביעית.
steps.simpleTranslation: For עבודה זרה, the source is what we already said. What is the source for שביעית?
steps.whatsHappening: Step 14 said both עבודה זרה and שביעית have a rule that their money takes on their status. The גמרא already gave the source for עבודה זרה, so now it asks for the source for שביעית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer in Step 14 only works if there really are two separate פסוקים. So the גמרא has to show where the שביעית rule is written. This question sets up the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The seventh year of the farming cycle, and the fruit that grows in it, which has special holiness
That which we already said
What is it? (What is its source?)

phrases.english: Idol worship: that is what we already said.
Shevi'is: what is its source?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the second source that Step 14's answer relies on
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק showing that money from שביעית fruit takes on שביעית status

steps.title: שביעית is compared to הקדש
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק calls the year 'holy', so שביעית passes its status to money just like הקדש does.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'It is a Jubilee, it shall be holy to you.' Just as holy property passes its holiness onto its money, so too שביעית passes its status onto its money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק that calls the year 'holy'. From that word it compares שביעית to הקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone knows that when הקדש is redeemed, its holiness moves onto the money. Since the תורה calls שביעית 'holy', its fruit works the same way, and money used to buy it gets שביעית status.

keyTerms.meaning: Holy property dedicated to the בית המקדש (הקדש)
Grabs onto its money: its status passes to the money paid for it
The fiftieth year (Jubilee)

phrases.english: "It is a Jubilee, it shall be holy to you":
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:12. The פסוק is about יובל, but the גמרא applies it to שביעית, which has the same rules.

phrases.english: just as holy property grabs onto its money,
so too Shevi'is grabs onto its money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 15's question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word 'קודש' compares שביעית to הקדש, which passes its status to its money

steps.title: Then should the שביעית fruit lose its holiness, like הקדש does?
steps.stepSummary: If שביעית is like הקדש, the original fruit should become ordinary once its status passes to the money.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if so, just as holy property passes its holiness to the money and itself becomes ordinary, so too שביעית fruit should pass its status to the money and itself become ordinary!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes the comparison further. With הקדש, once the holiness moves to the money, the item itself becomes plain חולין. Should שביעית fruit also become plain?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A comparison usually carries over the whole rule. With הקדש the holiness moves; it is not copied. So if we compare fully, the שביעית fruit should lose its status once it is traded.

keyTerms.meaning: Goes out to being ordinary: loses its holy status
Ordinary, non-holy items

phrases.aramaic: אִי מָה קוֹדֶשׁ תּוֹפֵס אֶת דָּמָיו
phrases.english: If so, just as holy property grabs onto its money
and itself goes out to be ordinary,
so too Shevi'is should grab onto its money
and itself go out to be ordinary?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מָה קוֹדֶשׁ תּוֹפֵס אֶת דָּמָיו וְיוֹצֵא לְחוּלִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how far the comparison in Step 16 goes
steps.kashyaTarget: The full comparison of שביעית to הקדש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the comparison is complete, the original fruit should lose its status, just as redeemed הקדש does

steps.title: The word 'shall be' keeps the fruit forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The word 'תהיה' teaches that the שביעית fruit stays as it was, even after its status passes to the money.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'shall be': it stays in its original state.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers from another word in the same פסוק. 'It shall be' means the fruit keeps its status.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So שביעית is only partly like הקדש. The status does spread to the money, but the original fruit does not become plain. Now there are two forbidden items, the fruit and the money.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches
It shall remain as it is

steps.confusionAlert: With הקדש the holiness moves from the item to the money. With שביעית it is copied: the money gets the status and the fruit keeps it too.

phrases.english: The verse says: "shall be":
as it is, so it shall stay.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 17's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: A separate word in the פסוק limits the comparison
steps.terutzHavaAmina: שביעית fruit loses its status once traded, like הקדש
steps.terutzMaskana: The fruit keeps its status, and the money also gets it

steps.title: How the status passes down a chain of trades
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that the first item and the newest trade are forbidden, while the items in between become permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does this work? If he bought meat with שביעית fruit, both the fruit and the meat must be removed at the time of ביעור. If he then bought fish with the meat, the meat leaves the status and the fish takes it. If he bought wine with the fish, the fish leaves and the wine takes it. If he bought oil with the wine, the wine leaves and the oil takes it. So what is the rule? Each newest item takes the שביעית status, and the original fruit itself stays forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an example of the rule it just learned. It follows the שביעית status through several trades.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The original fruit always stays forbidden because of 'תהיה'. The money or item traded for it works like הקדש: when it is traded again, its status moves on to the next item. At any moment only two things are forbidden: the original fruit and the newest item.

keyTerms.meaning: Must be removed at the time of ביעור (when that kind of fruit is no longer in the fields)
Left: lost the status
Entered: took on the status
Each latest one in the chain

phrases.english: How so? If he bought meat with Shevi'is fruit:
both these and those must be removed in Shevi'is.
If he bought fish with the meat:
the meat goes out and the fish come in.
If he bought wine with the fish:
the fish go out and the wine comes in.
If he bought oil with the wine:
the wine goes out and the oil comes in.

phrases.aramaic: הָא כֵּיצַד? אַחֲרוֹן אַחֲרוֹן נִתְפָּס בַּשְּׁבִיעִית,
phrases.english: So how is it? Each last one is caught by Shevi'is,
and the fruit itself stays forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how the rules of Steps 16 and 18 work in practice
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The original fruit and the latest item traded are forbidden; items in between lose the status
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the two rules working together: the money takes on the status like הקדש, but the fruit stays forbidden because of 'תהיה'.

steps.title: What about the view that two similar פסוקים do teach other cases?
steps.stepSummary: Step 14's answer only works for the view that two similar פסוקים do not teach other cases. What about the opposite view?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works for the one who says two such פסוקים do not teach other cases. But according to the one who says they do teach, what can be said?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges its own answer from Step 14. That answer depends on a rule that not everyone accepts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some hold that when two פסוקים teach the same thing, we do learn other cases from them. By that view, עבודה זרה and שביעית together should teach that money from every forbidden item is forbidden. Then the קידושין in the משנה should not work.

keyTerms.meaning: This works well
They do not teach (other cases)
What can be said?

phrases.english: This works for the one who says they do not teach,
phrases.notes: He means two פסוקים that teach the same rule, here עבודה זרה and שביעית.

phrases.english: but according to the one who says they do teach,
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנִיחָא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר אֵין מְלַמְּדִין אֶלָּא לְמַאן דְּאָמַר מְלַמְּדִין מַאי אִיכָּא לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges whether Step 14's answer works for every view
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer of Step 14 (two פסוקים that teach the same thing do not teach other cases)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: By the view that such פסוקים do teach, money from all forbidden items should be forbidden

steps.title: Both פסוקים have limiting words
steps.stepSummary: The words 'הוא' and 'היא' limit the money rule to עבודה זרה and שביעית alone.
steps.simpleTranslation: Two limiting words are written. Here it says 'for it is banned', and there it says 'it is a Jubilee'. 'It': yes. Anything else: no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that both פסוקים have a limiting word, 'it'. That word keeps the rule from spreading to other forbidden items.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even those who usually learn from two פסוקים agree when the תורה itself limits them. 'הוא' by עבודה זרה and 'היא' by שביעית mean that only these items pass their status to money. So money from other forbidden items is permitted, and the קידושין in the משנה works.

keyTerms.meaning: Limiting words in a פסוק
Banned, forbidden item
Anything else

steps.whatToRemember: Money from forbidden items is usually permitted, so קידושין with it works. Only עבודה זרה and שביעית pass their status to money, and the תורה limits the rule to them with the words 'הוא' and 'היא'.

phrases.english: [Two] limiting words are written,
phrases.notes: The word 'two' in square brackets is added in the corrected text.

phrases.english: it is written here: "For it is banned,"
and it is written there: "It is a Jubilee":
"it," yes; anything else, no.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 20's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting words in the פסוקים block learning to other cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: By the view that two פסוקים teach, money from all forbidden items is forbidden
steps.terutzMaskana: The words 'הוא' and 'היא' limit the rule, so other forbidden money is permitted

steps.title: A ישראל can betroth with holy gifts
steps.stepSummary: The משנה rules that betrothal with תרומות, מעשרות, מתנות, מי חטאת or אפר חטאת works, even when a ישראל does it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If a man betroths a woman with תרומה, מעשר, the priestly gifts, the water of purification or the ashes of purification, she is betrothed, even if he is a regular ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists holy items that a person cannot freely use, and says they still work for קידושין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ישראל cannot eat תרומה or the priestly gifts himself. Still, the משנה says his קידושין with them works. The גמרא will now ask what money value he actually has in these items.

keyTerms.meaning: One who betroths a woman
The portion of produce given to a כהן
Tithes, the tenth portions of produce
The priestly gifts from an animal: foreleg, cheeks and stomach
The water and red-heifer ashes used to purify someone who became impure from a dead body

phrases.english: MISHNA:
One who betroths a woman with terumot and with tithes,
and with the priestly gifts, and with the water of purification,
and with the ashes of purification —
she is betrothed, and this is so even if he is an Israelite.
phrases.notes: "Even an Israelite" means even a man who is not a כהן or לוי and can't use these gifts himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה and a new topic after the discussion of the money rule for עבודה זרה and שביעית.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קידושין done with תרומות, מעשרות, מתנות, מי חטאת or אפר חטאת is valid, even when done by a ישראל.

steps.title: עולא: the right to choose is not money
steps.stepSummary: עולא rules that טובת הנאה, the owner's right to pick which כהן or לוי gets the gift, has no money value.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא says: the benefit of choosing who gets the gift is not counted as money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens with a ruling from עולא about the value of the owner's right to choose the recipient of his gifts.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An owner of produce must give תרומה to a כהן, but he gets to decide which כהן. Someone might pay him for that choice, but עולא says this right is not real money. If so, it cannot be used for קידושין.

keyTerms.meaning: The benefit of choosing which כהן or לוי receives one's gifts
It is not counted as money

steps.confusionAlert: טובת הנאה is not the gift itself. It is only the owner's right to decide who receives the gift.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Ulla says:
The benefit of discretion does not have monetary value.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר עוּלָּא: טוֹבַת הֲנָאָה אֵינָהּ מָמוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a ruling that seems to bear directly on how the משנה's ישראל could betroth with gifts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: טובת הנאה has no money value.

steps.title: רבי אבא challenges עולא from the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבא quotes the משנה: a ישראל can betroth with the gifts, which seems to show that his right to choose is worth money.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבא objected to עולא: the משנה says that if a man betroths with תרומות, מעשרות, gifts, purification water or red-heifer ashes, she is betrothed, even if he is a ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבא attacks עולא's ruling using our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ישראל cannot use these gifts himself. The only thing he seems to have is the right to choose who gets them. If his קידושין works, that right must be worth money, which goes against עולא.

keyTerms.meaning: He raised an objection to him from a source
Ashes of the red heifer

phrases.english: Rabbi Abba raised an objection to Ulla:
One who betroths with terumot, or with tithes,
or with gifts, with the water of purification, or with the ashes of the red heifer —
she is betrothed, and this is so even if he is an Israelite.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges עולא's ruling from Step 23 using the משנה in Step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: עולא's ruling that טובת הנאה is not money.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ישראל owns nothing in the gifts except the right to choose; since his קידושין works, that right must have money value.

steps.title: עולא: the ישראל inherited from a כהן grandfather
steps.stepSummary: עולא explains that the משנה is about a ישראל who inherited untithed produce from his mother's father, a כהן, so he truly owns the gifts inside it.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said to him: Here it is talking about a ישראל who inherited untithed produce from his mother's father, who was a כהן. And the משנה holds that gifts not yet separated are treated as if they were already separated.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא answers the challenge by setting the משנה in a special case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The grandfather was a כהן, so the תרומה inside his produce already belonged to him. The grandson inherits that ownership, not just a right to choose. So the ישראל betroths with something he really owns and can sell to a כהן, and עולא's rule stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Produce from which the required gifts have not yet been separated
His mother's father

keyTerms.term: מַתָּנוֹת שֶׁלֹּא הוּרְמוּ כְּמִי שֶׁהוּרְמוּ דָּמְיָין
keyTerms.meaning: Gifts not yet separated are treated as if already separated
Here, in this case

steps.confusionAlert: Why a mother's father? A grandson through a daughter of a כהן can be a ישראל, yet still inherit his grandfather's property.

phrases.english: He said to him: Here it is dealing with an Israelite
who came into possession of untithed produce
from the household of his mother's father, a priest.
And the Mishna holds: gifts that have not been separated
are considered as though they have been separated.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָכָא בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנָּפְלוּ לוֹ טְבָלִים מִבֵּית אֲבִי אִמּוֹ כֹּהֵן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבי אבא's challenge from Step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Setting the משנה in a narrow case (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ישראל in the משנה owns only the right to choose, so that right must be worth money.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ישראל inherited real ownership of the gifts from his כהן grandfather, so the משנה says nothing about the value of טובת הנאה.
steps.whatToRemember: עולא keeps his rule (טובת הנאה is not money) by placing the משנה in the case of an inheritance from a כהן grandfather.

steps.title: רבי חייא בר אבין asks: is the right to choose money?
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבין asks רב הונא whether טובת הנאה counts as money.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבין asked רב הונא: Is the benefit of choosing counted as money or not?
steps.whatsHappening: A new discussion opens with a straight question on the same issue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the question is asked openly, without assuming עולא's answer. This sets up רב הונא's reply in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked him
Is it money or is it not money?

phrases.aramaic: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין מֵרַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Hiyya bar Avin inquired of Rav Huna:

phrases.aramaic: טוֹבַת הֲנָאָה מָמוֹן אוֹ אֵינָהּ מָמוֹן?
phrases.english: Does the benefit of discretion have monetary value, or does it not?

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּעָא מִינֵּיהּ רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין מֵרַב הוּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises again the question עולא ruled on in Step 23, this time as an open question.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether טובת הנאה has money value.

steps.title: רב הונא: we already learned it in the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that the משנה shows it is money, since a ישראל can betroth with the gifts.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said to him: You already learned it: if a man betroths with תרומות, מעשרות, gifts, purification water or red-heifer ashes, she is betrothed, even if he is a ישראל!
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא answers the question by quoting our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא reads the משנה the same way רבי אבא did. A ישראל's קידושין works with the gifts, so his right to choose must be worth money.

keyTerms.meaning: You have already learned it in a source

phrases.english: He said to him: You learned it:
One who betroths with terumot or with tithes
or with gifts, with the water of purification, or with the ashes of the red heifer —
she is betrothed, and this is so even if he is an Israelite!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 26 by quoting the משנה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: טובת הנאה is money, as the משנה lets a ישראל betroth with the gifts.

steps.title: Rejecting רב הונא's proof with עולא's answer
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבין points out that the משנה was already explained as an inheritance from a כהן grandfather, so it proves nothing.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבין said to him: But didn't we already explain it as a ישראל who inherited untithed produce from his mother's father, a כהן?
steps.whatsHappening: The questioner pushes back on רב הונא's proof by recalling עולא's explanation of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא already showed that the משנה can be about a ישראל who really owns the gifts. So the משנה does not prove that the bare right to choose is worth money, and the question stays open.

keyTerms.meaning: Didn't we already set it in a specific case?

phrases.english: He said to him: But didn't we establish it as dealing with an Israelite
who came into possession of untithed produce
from the household of his mother's father, a priest?
phrases.notes: This is עולא's answer from Step 25, used again here.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְלָאו אוֹקֵימְנָא בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנָּפְלוּ לוֹ טְבָלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רב הונא's proof from Step 27 using עולא's case from Step 25.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects only the proof from the משנה, not necessarily רב הונא's view.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The משנה can be about a ישראל who truly inherited the gifts, so it says nothing about טובת הנאה.
steps.whatToRemember: Because of עולא's case, our משנה cannot settle whether טובת הנאה is money.
